newsitem.title: POLAND: PIONEER PDM SAYS POLAND'S KGHM SHARES WORTH PLN 32.
newsitem.headline: PIONEER PDM SAYS POLAND'S KGHM SHARES WORTH PLN 32.

text.p: Pioneer PDM brokerage estimated the current market value of the shares of the biggest Polish copper producer, KGHM Polska Miedz SA at 32 zlotys each, Pioneer said in a report.
KGHM, whose public offering ends on Friday, is the fifth world producer of electrolytic copper and a leading silver producer.

Pioneer said in a report dated June 30 that its estimate was a mean average of two estimates -- one based on comparisons with P/E ratios of copper producers listed in New York and another based on the method of discounting of future profits.
"The method of comparing ratios produced a value of 20 zlotys per share while the value of shares calculated by discounting future net profits is 44 zlotys," it said.
"The share value is assumed as the arithmetical value amounting to 32 zlotys," it added.

The growth of profits and book value would be determined in the long run by an annual 1.5 percent growth in world copper consumption, KGHM's 11 percent share in the European market and its 90 percent share in the domestic market, the report said.
The planned 26 percent reduction of production costs and the 12 percent increase in the copper production in the next four years should also bring good effects, Pioneer said.

It said the the risk of investing in the shares of KGHM resulted from the strong position of trade unions in the company, high production costs and comparatively low P/E ratios of copper companies listed on the New York Exchange.
